the current S2ST system can translate simultaneous speech at the sentence level with a reasonable degree of accuracy and can also handle some paralinguistic information such as emotions, but the current system cannot translate simultaneous speech at a discourse level.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have achieved simultaneous speech to speech translation for a limited domain, with a limited vocabulary, and with a limited number of languages.

the S2ST system can be built by combining three modules: speech recognition, machine translation and speech synthesis, and it is possible to achieve simultaneous speech translation with the current state-of-the-art technology.
we have developed a system which can translate a Japanese sentence to English sentence in real time with 30% word error rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the simultaneous nature of S2ST is a key to its success.
the simultaneous translation system can be improved by using the information from both the source and target languages.
we can build a system with a good degree of simultaneous speech translation by using the combination of a multilingual ASR and a multilingual MT.
